meta.name: Monitor website uptime and visual drift with Snapshot Site, Google Sheets and Slack

name: Website Uptime & Visual Check → Slack State-Change Alerts

parameters.content:
## Website Uptime & Visual Check → Slack State-Change Alerts

### How it works

Every 10 minutes this workflow reads a watchlist from a Google Sheet (`url`, `label`, `baselineUrl`, `lastState`) and loops over the pages one at a time, running a **two-stage gate** per page.

**Stage 1 (cheap) — is it up?** One Snapshot Site **Analyze** call with `enableQuality: true` and `enableSummary: false`. The quality bundle reports what a real browser saw — `httpStatus`, `isBlank`, `hasCaptcha` — so **Evaluate Availability** returns a verdict of `up` or `down` with a reason. No AI summary is requested: this is a health check, nobody reads a summary of it, and at 144 runs a day the saved latency and cost are the whole point.

**Stage 2 (expensive) — does it still look right?** The **Compare** call runs *only* on a page stage 1 proved is up: stored baseline image as `beforeUrl`, live page as `afterUrl`. Pixel-comparing a page that is down would burn a Compare call to rediscover a 503 that stage 1 already reported.

**Detect State Change** then compares the computed state (`up` / `down` / `visual-drift`) against the row's `lastState` and alerts **only on a transition** — up → down, down → up, up → visual-drift and back. Recoveries are announced too. Every run writes `lastState` and `lastCheckedAt` back to the sheet, on both the changed and the unchanged path, so the next sweep has a fresh reference. If a run cannot determine a state (empty `quality` object, unreadable response) the previous value is **kept**, never overwritten with a guess.

### Setup steps

- Install the `n8n-nodes-snapshot-site` community node (Settings → Community nodes → Install → `n8n-nodes-snapshot-site`) — verified by n8n.
- Add a Snapshot Site credential, a Google Sheets credential, and a Slack credential.
- Create a **Watchlist** tab and type this header row literally into row 1, one column per cell: `url`, `label`, `baselineUrl`, `lastState`, `lastCheckedAt`. Cell **A1 must contain the literal text `url`**, not a URL — otherwise Google Sheets' `read` operation treats that URL as the column name, `$json.url` is `undefined` for every row and every call fails with the soft error `URL is required` (confirmed live).
- Fill one row per page: `url` = the live page, `label` = a short human name for alerts, `baselineUrl` = a hosted screenshot of the page as it should look. Leave `lastState` and `lastCheckedAt` empty — the workflow fills them in. All URLs need the scheme (`https://…`); the API rejects bare domains.
- Point **Read Uptime Watchlist** and **Update Watchlist State** at your spreadsheet and tab, attach the Snapshot Site credential to both Snapshot Site nodes, and set the channel on **Notify State Change on Slack**.
- After import, open **Update Watchlist State** and switch its Mapping Column Mode to **"Map Automatically"** — Google Sheets column mappings are a resourceMapper parameter and never survive a JSON import, regardless of what the JSON says.

### Customization

Tune `VISUAL_DRIFT_PERCENT` in **Evaluate Visual Drift** (10% = layout drift; use `> 0` for pages where a single character matters, ~30 for defacement), or mask dynamic regions with `hide` selectors on `afterOptions` instead of raising the band. Change the cadence on the trigger, add states of your own (a `slow` state, a `captcha` state) by extending the `VALID` list in **Detect State Change**, or fan a second branch off **Check for State Change** that pages on-call only for `down` transitions while drift stays Slack-only.

## Schedule and read the watchlist

Runs every 10 minutes and reads every watched page from the Google Sheet (`url`, `label`, `baselineUrl`, `lastState`).
The loop processes one page per iteration and every branch returns to it, so one failing URL can never abort the sweep.
The Done branch ends on a No Operation node: alerts are per-page state changes, so there is no digest to build.

## Stage 1 (cheap): is the page up?

One Analyze call per page with `enableQuality: true` and `enableSummary: false` — `httpStatus`, `isBlank` and `hasCaptcha` decide `up` vs `down`. `forceRefresh: true` because a cached analysis would report an earlier sweep's health and defeat the 10-minute cadence.
Hard failures (error output) and soft failures (`{error: true}` on the success output) both become a `down` record with the API's own message and go straight to the state comparison — never aborting, never reaching stage 2.
If the `quality` object comes back empty, the state is left blank on purpose: undetermined is not the same as up.

## Stage 2 (expensive) + state-change alerting

Compare runs only for a page stage 1 proved is up — stored baseline as `beforeUrl`, live page as `afterUrl`. Never pixel-compare a page that is down.
**Detect State Change** alerts only on a transition (up → down, down → up, up → visual-drift, and back). At 144 runs a day, alerting on state instead of on change means 144 identical messages and a muted channel.
Both the changed and the unchanged path write `lastState` + `lastCheckedAt` back to the sheet, so the next run always has a fresh reference. An undetermined run keeps the previous value instead of inventing one.
